UPDATE 76 (2026-09-22, early — THE CIR-EMISSION ARC IS MERGED, plus the __builtin_constant_p slice. develop = b659a4b97, PUSHED. master b2b486a79 / v0.100.0 unchanged.)

*** BOTH MERGES ARE DONE AND THE LANES ARE RECORDED. Nothing is half-landed. `bash scripts/lane_ledger.sh check --promote` returns rc=0 at develop. ***

▶ WHAT MERGED — two waves.

 WAVE 1, the CIR-emission arc (merge 9356159f7, 9 commits). Seven fixes, each its own commit, each with a reducer verified against BOTH gcc and clang:
   fa35f914e a POINTER typedef must not hoist its struct's member deps above itself
   87aac8fba an array compound literal's POINTER element keeps its star
   a14359729 a NESTED aggregate member keeps the typedef alias it was spelled with
   eadc99410 an enum-typed `static` keeps internal linkage        [SILENT WRONG ANSWER]
   8268d059c macro paint is PER-REGION, not per whole replacement [deletes a 46-line heuristic]
   10030e135 postfix ++/-- binds TIGHTER than a cast
   3c9adf420 a call's `(` binds by ADJACENCY, not by an empty opStack [SILENT WRONG ANSWER]
 plus the c-torture baseline ruling and the lane records.

 WAVE 2, the __builtin_constant_p slice (merge b659a4b97, commit a8f22d1be). It answered 0 for EVERY operand because it was a preprocessor macro whose body was literally `0` — the operand was never consulted. Now a parse-time builtin in the expression arm beside __builtin_classify_type (which stopped being a macro for exactly this reason), asking madc's ONE constant evaluator parse_constant_integer_expression, with TokenBase::is_constant() as the fallback for string/real literals. That is what makes `(1234 + 45) & ~7` answer 1 although it is not a literal token. tests/testbuiltinconstantp.mad pins BOTH halves — answering 1 for a variable would make every glibc constant-gated branch lie in the opposite direction, which is WORSE than always-0.

▶ THE LAST FIX OF WAVE 1 IS THE ONE TO UNDERSTAND. `d->ok && d->rdr (&t, 1, d->aux) == 0` died on "Malformed expression: 2 operands with no operator between them" (mir-reduce.h:430). The member and subscript fn-ptr call arms gated on `!opstack_has_pending_op` — "has any tighter-than-assignment operator been pushed" — as a PROXY for the real question, adjacency. A call is POSTFIX; it binds tighter than any binary operator, so a pending operator says nothing. With `&&` pending the arm declined, the `(` became a grouping paren, and the argument list parsed as a comma expression. WITHOUT a trailing comparison the same root was SILENT: the call was dropped and the function POINTER became the operand (`d.ok + d.rdr (21)` returned an address where gcc returns 43). The adjacency question already had ONE owner in the same function — paren_binds_to_receiver, written for the functor arm with the note "We do NOT gate on opstack_has_pending_op" — scoped inside a block where the siblings could not reach it. Hoisted; both arms adopt it.

▶ WHERE MIR STANDS NOW (measured with -D_DEFAULT_SOURCE):
   c2mir.c      12,041 lines  CLEAN — a valid 2 MB ELF relocatable exporting the full API
   mir-gen.c    10,520 lines  CLEAN
   mir.c         7,474 lines  CLEAN  <- closed by 3c9adf420; this was UPDATE 75's NEXT (1)
   mir-debug-gdb.c  138 lines  CLEAN
   mir-debug.c   3,456 lines  FRONT END CLEAN; stops at MIR item registration (see NEXT 1)
 Reproduce any of them: bin/madc --std=c17 -D_DEFAULT_SOURCE -Ithird_party/mir -Ithird_party/mir/c2mir -c -o /tmp/x.o third_party/mir/<file>

▶ NEXT, in order:

 (1) THE mir.arg_memcpy EMBEDDING COLLISION — the real self-hosting blocker, because it applies at LINK time to all five objects. "MIR error: _MIR_builtin_func: func mir.arg_memcpy has already another address". NOT a compiler defect. `mir.arg_memcpy` is an asm() LABEL naming a MIR item in ctx->environment_module (mir.c:82 — PER-CONTEXT, not a process global; I checked, a first guess that it was global was wrong). Three sites touch the name: mir-gen-x86_64.c:548 registers it bound to libc memcpy via _MIR_builtin_func; mir-gen-x86_64.c:795 aliases it for AOT linking; mir-debug.c:2556/2569 declares it weak in an objload table. The registrar refuses a second address for one name (mir.c:4621-4624). madc EMBEDS libmir, so while it compiles mir-debug.c its own generator has already registered the name in that context and the TU declares the same label resolving elsewhere. FIX DIRECTION (a design call, make it deliberately): keep the compiled program's MIR context separate from the one madc uses for its own gen work, or resolve a target-declared name that collides with a gen builtin as an ordinary symbol instead of routing it through _MIR_builtin_func.

 (2) EIGHT MISSING asm()-LABEL ALIAS EXPORTS, measured by object-diffing madc against gcc -std=gnu17 for the same TU:
       c2mir.c  gcc 47 global text symbols, madc 41 — missing __mir_addoti, __mir_uaddoti, __mir_suboti, __mir_usuboti, __mir_muloti, __mir_umuloti (mir-int128-helper.h:302-315)
       mir.c    gcc 151, madc 149 — missing mir.va_arg, mir.va_block_arg (mir-x86_64.c:154,156)
     (UPDATE 75 said 44 for c2mir.c; that was wrong, it is 41.) All eight are `extern __typeof(F) F_export asm("name") __attribute__((alias("F")))`. madc's var_emit_name redirects REFERENCES through the asm name but never emits the alias SYMBOL. Irrelevant to compiling, LOAD-BEARING for linking a madc-built libmir — MIR's generated code calls mir.va_arg for varargs and the __mir_*oti helpers for 128-bit overflow.

 (3) NO `--std=gnu*` EXISTS. madc offers c89/c90/c99/c11/c17/c23, c++NN, madc. MIR needs -D_DEFAULT_SOURCE passed by hand. Per invariant I1 this belongs in the --std=/LanguageStd registry, not a flag users must know.

 (4) headerless-win (promote=no) carries TWO KNOWN FAILURES: tests/testimplicitlibcproto.mad + its c17 twin. The win64 pack serves NO prototype for printf, so an undeclared call falls back to `extern int printf();` where the linux pack yields `extern int printf(char *p0, ...)`. Classified PRE-EXISTING against the PUBLISHED v0.100.0 windows artifact, which emits the identical line. KG Gap win64_pack_serves_no_libc_prototype. The lane also still needs a ratchet baseline like the others; giving it one edits scripts/ (CODE_PATHS) so it rides a code wave.

 (5) Still banked, untouched: the polyglot S0 seam (docs/plans/2026-09-21-polyglot-front-ends-typescript-first.md §12's four owner questions, the load-bearing one being the `string` representation); the REPL arc; the headerless-win .win64_expect twin; the embedding docs gap; the AGENTS.md dangling knowledge-graph.md index entry; 28 root scratch files.

▶ METHOD NOTES WORTH KEEPING.
 (a) THE bcp-1.c FALSE GREEN is the lesson of this session. The gcc-torture lane went RED on bcp-1.c right after the call-binding fix, which LOOKS exactly like a regression. It was the opposite: the test had been passing only because the dropped call made `! (*good_t0[i])()` evaluate `!` against a non-null function POINTER, skipping its abort(). Two bugs cancelling, and the two loops' opposite polarity is what hid it — the bad loops had no pending operator, so those calls were real. Classified by running the PRE-ARC binary at /workspace/madc-bisect (204a442ae, an ancestor of HEAD): it already printed 0 for __builtin_constant_p(1) exactly as HEAD did, while `! (*tab[i])(5)` there assigned the pointer to an int and SIGSEGVd. A RED that appears the moment you fix something deserves that classification BEFORE it is called a regression.
 (b) The emit-C oracle made the whole arc tractable: `--emit=c11` (writes STDOUT, IGNORES -o) piped to `gcc -std=c17 -w -fsyntax-only`.
 (c) Object-diffing madc against gcc for the same TU (nm, symbol counts, linkage letters) found two defects no suite would catch — the enum-static linkage leak and the missing alias exports.
 (d) Pre-building EVERY toolchain before the seam battery paid off again: host -O0, release -O2, MinGW hosted + release PE, macOS x86-64 + arm64 all built green before a single suite ran, so no late -O2 / LLP64 / clang-only finding cost a cycle.
 (e) TWO ERRORS THAT ARE NOT madc's, do not chase them: `va_list` at mir.h:771 and `conflicting types for MIR_interp_arr_varg` are STRICT-c17 artifacts (gcc -std=c17 rejects the same lines); mir-x86_64.c:154,156's asm() labels are REJECTED by gcc -std=c17 and ACCEPTED by madc.

known_pre_existing_gaps: SCRIPT `value` IS NOT YET THE 32-BYTE madc_value STRUCT (recorded 2026-08-17, owner: not to be taken on now). Symptom: `value f()` returned BY VALUE emits `int f()` and silently returns nothing (exit 0, empty output) — func_def's return-type arm -> type_list -> append_type_specs has no dtARRAY case and falls through to int. That is why php::print_r returns madc::value & rather than madc::value. CORRECTED PREMISE: a C type DOES exist — madc_value (include/madc_api.h:52) is a tagged 32-byte aligned(16) struct, and madc::value merely CONTAINS it plus two unique_ptr members (32+8+8 = 48 = the emitted long long[6]); the opaque-buffer lowering exists because of those OWNING C++ members, not a missing type. MEASURED: _array/_object are private with no friends and all 40 refs are in ONE file (src/madc_value.cpp) — 12 mutations, 28 reads; the cell finalizer is already wired and called from generated code (cir_builder.cpp:25789/25797); the is_array_object sites would mostly RETIRE. HARD PART: the class deep-copies the containers while the cell path shares, so the migration needs copy-on-write at those 12 sites — a semantic change with its own oracled tests. Full write-up: docs/plans/2026-06-12-type-table-value-abi-design.md section 9. Sibling defect, also open: assigning to a `value &` PARAMETER is wrongly rejected ('assignment of incompatible value').

VLA NOT DEALLOCATED ON BACKWARD GOTO: a `goto` jumping back to before a VLA's declaration must deallocate the VLA (gcc/C semantics; gcc-torture 20040811-1.c). madc lowers VLAs as malloc + __attribute__((cleanup)), which frees only on SCOPE EXIT, not on the backward goto re-entering the scope — so a backward-goto loop over a VLA LEAKS one allocation per iteration. 20040811-1.c leaks ~2GB over 1e6 iterations; it passes only when memory is available (it OOM-SIGSEGV'd when the MIR fork's 128MB code-holder reservation reduced headroom — see mir_fork; arch-gated off x86-64, so it passes again). Proper fix: free the VLA at the backward goto. Separate future slice.
